name: Full Stack Developer
description: Entry-level full stack developer shipping a feature end to end: UI, API and database.

skills.name: Frontend Fundamentals
skills.description: JavaScript, a UI library such as React, state, rendering and responsive CSS.

L1: Names the exact components, hooks and styles used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains that a state update schedules a re-render and what triggers it
Explains how the event loop orders promises before timers
Explains how flexbox and grid differ and when each fits
L3: Explains when they would NOT lift state up or use a global store, and the cost
Defends a rendering approach (client vs server) against a concrete alternative with a real cost of each

skills.name: REST API Design
skills.description: Designing HTTP APIs: resources, methods, status codes, idempotency, pagination, versioning and authentication.

L1: Names the exact endpoints, methods and payloads used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains which HTTP methods are safe and idempotent and why that matters for retries
Explains how 401 differs from 403 and 400 from 422
Explains how cursor pagination differs from offset pagination
L3: Explains when they would NOT use REST (for example streaming or very chatty clients) and what they would use instead
Defends an API versioning or authentication choice against a concrete alternative with a real cost of each

skills.name: SQL & Data Modelling
skills.description: Relational modelling, joins, indexes, transactions and query performance.

L1: Names the exact tables, queries and schema used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains what an index speeds up and what it costs on writes
Explains the difference between INNER and LEFT JOIN with an example
Explains what a transaction guarantees (atomicity, isolation) and a bug it prevents
L3: Explains when they would denormalize or NOT add an index, and the trade-off
Defends SQL vs a document store for their data with a real cost of each
Explains how they found and fixed a slow query (EXPLAIN, index, rewrite)

skills.name: Auth Across the Stack
skills.description: Signing users in end to end: login UI, tokens or cookies, protected routes and server checks.

L1: Names the exact login flow and where the user is checked used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains where the server must verify the user and why hiding a button in the UI is not security
Explains how cookies and tokens are sent and the risk of each
Explains what CORS blocks and what it does not
L3: Explains when they would NOT trust data sent by the client and what they re-check on the server
Defends cookie sessions vs bearer tokens for their app with a real cost of each

skills.name: Testing
skills.description: Writing reliable automated tests: unit, integration, mocking and what to test.

L1: Names the exact tests and the tool used to run them used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains the difference between a unit test and an integration test with an example from their project
Explains what a mock or stub replaces and the risk of over-mocking
Explains how they made a flaky test reliable
L3: Explains what they chose NOT to test and why
Defends their test mix (unit vs integration) against a concrete alternative with a real cost of each

skills.name: Deploying a Full Stack App
skills.description: Hosting the frontend and backend, environment config, and basic monitoring.

L1: Names the exact hosting and pipeline for each part used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains how the frontend finds the API in each environment
Explains what must never be shipped in the frontend bundle
Explains how they know when production is failing
L3: Explains when they would NOT split the frontend and backend hosting, and the cost
Defends their hosting choice against a concrete alternative with a real cost of each

skills.name: Git & Collaboration
skills.description: Version control workflow: branching, merging, rebasing, pull requests, and recovering from mistakes.

L1: Names the exact git commands and branching workflow used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains the difference between merge and rebase and what each does to history
Explains how to resolve a merge conflict step by step
Explains how revert differs from reset
L3: Explains when they would NOT rebase (shared branches) and the cost of rewriting history
Defends a branching strategy (trunk-based vs feature branches) against the alternative for a team of their size
